titel: Hotel near the Overloon War Museum | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Stay a 9-minute drive from the Overloon War Museum. Book the War Museum package with admission, dinner and breakfast, or unwind after the museum in the wellness area at Hotel Asteria.
hero-sub: The oldest Second World War museum in Western Europe, a 9-minute drive from your hotel room in Venray.
hero-alt: B-25 Mitchell bomber in the military hall of the Overloon War Museum
oog-kop: The Overloon War Museum at a glance
t2-waarde: Mon-Fri 10 am-5 pm, Sat-Sun 11 am-5 pm (2026)
v1-p1: From Hotel Asteria it is a 9-minute drive to the Overloon War Museum (Oorlogsmuseum Overloon). The museum stands in a wooded park on the site where the Battle of Overloon was fought in the autumn of 1944. It began on 26 September and lasted until 18 October. More than a thousand soldiers were killed.
v1-p2: A little over eighteen months later, on 25 May 1946, the museum opened on the initiative of Harrie van Daal from Overloon. It was the first war museum in Western Europe. The museum recommends allowing three to four hours for a visit.
v1-alt: T-34 tank among the trees in the museum park at Overloon
v2-p1: The museum tells the story of the war in a series of permanent exhibitions. In the exhibition on the Netherlands in the Second World War you follow eight people through the years of occupation. D-DEX is a 4D experience of D-Day on Omaha Beach. The large military hall holds the vehicles and aircraft, and the Lancaster Pavilion houses a British bomber reconstructed from more than 2000 pieces of wreckage.
v2-p2: A special feature is the cycle bridge: ninety metres long, running three metres above the floor straight through the military hall. During opening hours you can cycle across it free of charge. Good to know: some parts use light and sound effects, and the stories can be moving.
v2-alt: The Hercules bridgelayer in the military hall of the museum
v3-p1: If you want to follow the story of 1944 further, there are two war cemeteries in the area. Near Ysselsteyn lies the only German war cemetery in the Netherlands, with 31,813 graves on 28 hectares and a visitor centre with a free exhibition. On the Hoenderstraat in Venray is Venray War Cemetery, where 692 Commonwealth servicemen are buried. Most of them were killed during the Battle of Overloon.
v3-alt: Rows of grave crosses at the German War Cemetery in Ysselsteyn
tip: Go outside the school holidays and start after lunch, from 1 pm. According to the museum it is quietest then, and you still have just enough time for a visit. Wear comfortable shoes: from the car park it is a 350-metre walk through the museum park to the entrance.
g1-tekst: From 10 am to 5 pm on weekdays and from 11 am to 5 pm at weekends. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December.
g1-alt: The entrance of the Overloon War Museum with bunker domes
g2-tekst: €20 at the ticket desk, €18.50 online. With the Museumkaart, the Dutch museum pass, entry is free.
g2-alt: The Sherman tank After Hitler in the museum
g3-tekst: About a hundred spaces and two charging points on the Bergkampweg. Then a 350-metre walk through the park.
g3-alt: Steel bridge in the autumn woods of the museum park
g4-tekst: Dogs on a lead are welcome. Free wheelchairs are available at the reception desk and the museum is largely on one level.
g4-alt: Horsa glider in the military hall
dag-kop: How to make a day of it
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, a day at the museum, and then time to let it all sink in, in the sauna and at the table.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 am to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 am to 10.30 am at weekends. The museum opens at 10 am, at weekends at 11 am.
m2-tekst: Allow three to four hours for the exhibitions and the military hall. For coffee with vlaai or lunch, Museumcafé De Vrijheid is by the entrance.
m2-alt: Humber armoured car at the Overloon War Museum
m3-tekst: Nine minutes later you are back in Venray. In the sauna you can let the impressions of the day settle. The wellness area is open from 4 pm to 10 pm Monday to Thursday and from 12 noon to 10 pm Friday to Sunday. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m4-tekst: The day ends at a table in the hotel brasserie, where you can have dinner until 9.30 pm. With the package, the three-course dinner is included.
arr-regel: Museum, dinner and overnight stay arranged in one go. We give you your admission ticket, and in the evening you take your seat in the brasserie.
arr-vink3: Admission to the Overloon War Museum
arr-vink4: Coffee or tea at the museum
arr-alt: Military vehicle in a reconstructed beach scene at the Overloon War Museum
kaart-regel: The museum lies north-west of Venray. The war cemeteries in Ysselsteyn and Venray are also on the map.
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, the Overloon War Museum, the two war cemeteries and ZooParc Overloon
f1-v: How far is the Overloon War Museum from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 5.8 kilometres to the museum car park, about 9 minutes by car. By bike it is 5.6 kilometres, around 25 minutes. You can hire bikes and e-bikes at our reception. Please note: there are no buses to the museum at weekends.
f2-v: What is included in the War Museum package?
f2-a: An overnight stay with breakfast buffet, your admission to the Overloon War Museum, coffee or tea at the museum and a three-course dinner in the hotel brasserie. Use the button with the package to choose your date and see the price.
f3-v: How long does a visit to the museum take?
f3-a: The museum recommends allowing three to four hours. If you start after lunch, you will be back in good time for the wellness area and dinner at the hotel.
f4-v: Is there a temporary exhibition at the moment?
f4-a: Yes. Until 2 May 2027 you can see Hitler en de Macht van het Beeld (Hitler and the Power of the Image): thirty photographs from archives around the world, with a short film about propaganda.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog to the museum?
f5-a: Yes, dogs on a lead are welcome in the museum and in the museum café.
f6-v: Can I visit the German War Cemetery in Ysselsteyn on the same day?
f6-a: Yes. The cemetery is open all year and is a 17-minute drive from the hotel, in the opposite direction from the museum. According to the museum, it is about a quarter of an hour by car from the museum.

slot-tekst: Nine minutes from Overloon, your room, the wellness area on the Top Floor and a table in the brasserie are waiting for you.

ysselsteyn.desc: The only German military cemetery in the Netherlands. On 28 hectares lie 31,813 dead, almost all in a grave of their own. The cemetery is maintained by the Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgräberfürsorge and is open all year. In the visitor centre, opened in 2021, a free exhibition tells the history of the site and of the lives behind the crosses. Parking is available on site.
ysselsteyn.credit: Photos: FakirNL via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.

venraywar.desc: On the Hoenderstraat in Venray, 692 Commonwealth servicemen are buried. The graves date from October 1944 to March 1945. Most were killed near Venray during the Battle of Overloon. The cemetery is maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, and since 2020 graves can be adopted through a foundation in Venray.
